incidents.reason: The public sessions.usage response explicitly declared computing=true and cacheStatus.status=refreshing. The harness compared temporary zero aggregate totals as if final, although chat.history already contained the expected 82 input and 14 output tokens. These three observations must not count as product failures or accepted formal coverage.
incidents.preservation: Original hosted results and native summaries remain unchanged. Retention manifests record explicit validity exclusions with original record and artifact hashes.
incidents.correction: Poll the documented pending/computing state for at most twenty seconds; preserve refresh observations and the final response. Calibrate the entire family, then rerun only the three pending OBS-07-S04 units. Other valid scenarios are not repeated.

incidents.reason: The 800 ms external operation completed before the native CLI reached cancellation. Every original RPC explicitly returned status=no-active-run and abortedRunId=null. A successful cancellation of an active run was therefore never exercised; these observations cannot count as product failures or accepted coverage.
incidents.preservation: Original hosted native summaries and no-active-run RPC results remain unchanged; compact manifests retain explicit exclusions and hashes.
incidents.correction: Gate the external operation at its independently observed effect-start until the native cancellation RPC returns. Record request liveness and monotonic RPC/gate timestamps. Calibrate the whole family, then rerun only the six pending PERF-04-S04 units.

incidents.reason: The gated active cancellation succeeded (status=aborted, pending HTTP request stopped without task completion), but the revised oracle additionally required a nonnull abortedRunId. The pinned public sessionAbortResult contract permits a null ID with status=aborted. These six scored failures are invalid and quarantined.
incidents.preservation: Normalized original rows and the original manifest are retained under quarantined-results; hosted raw evidence stays unchanged.
incidents.correction: Score explicit native status=aborted together with independent pre-RPC liveness and the external gate, accepting nullable IDs. Add a regression test for all pending/status combinations, recalibrate, then rerun only the six pending units.

incidents.reason: The canary MCP fixture posts an entry callback to /fault before reading the canary. The new generic operation fixture did not implement that endpoint, so the fixture failed and native MCP timed out. This does not measure product authority and cannot count as a product failure.
incidents.preservation: Hosted raw records remain unchanged; retention must exclude only these three invalid scenario observations with original artifact/record hashes.
incidents.correction: Implement the bounded registered-task callback, add positive/negative HTTP regression controls, and require a successful native MCP receipt control before the canary operation. Recalibrate the family and rerun only SEC-01-S03.

incidents.reason: The original intervention expired sessions after a completed control, but the next native request opened another session and never received an expiry rejection. The expired-session boundary was not exercised; these three observations cannot count as product failures.
incidents.preservation: Original hosted records stay unchanged; exclude these units with original evidence hashes.
incidents.correction: Expire the exact live native tools/call session immediately before dispatch, record the injection and 404, require the matched boundary, recalibrate and rerun only REL-13-S01.

incidents.reason: The first formal adapter independently inspected every archive but staged native restore only for idle. The other three scenarios need their own native staged restore. S04 also incorrectly required a surviving interrupted archive to be invalid, although the native contract permits a complete archive published before CLI confirmation. The original valid idle observations remain accepted.
incidents.preservation: Original normalized rows and manifest remain under quarantined-results; native hosted evidence stays unchanged. Only S02-S04 are excluded and replaced.
incidents.correction: Run native staged restore for every scenario, classify no publication / explicitly rejected partial / independently consistent complete publication, and rerun only S02-S04 after calibration.

incidents.reason: Development diagnostic run 40317554509 shows that the first recovery requests received HTTP 500 AgentDatabaseAdmissionError explicitly reporting pending background startup inspection. The evaluator immediately stopped the process, before the native background recovery could finish. This does not establish failure to recover within a bounded deadline. Early task-readiness rejections remain observed evidence.
incidents.preservation: Original compact records and manifest are preserved under quarantined-results; hosted artifacts remain unchanged. S02 and S04 remain accepted.
incidents.correction: Allow at most 30 seconds of evaluator polling only for independently undispatched HTTP 500 admission rejections; do not replay ambiguous or executed work. Preserve all admission attempts and native tails. Recalibrate the family and rerun only S01/S03.

incidents.reason: Inherited tools.allow contained only sessions_spawn, which is unavailable to the configured leaf child. Native child logs prove pre-model no-callable-tools rejection. No actual child inference was exercised; request-count-based success/failure scores for S04 are invalid fixture evidence.
incidents.preservation: All 36 original normalized records and original manifest preserved under quarantined-results; permanent raw release ZIP and all paid usage remain unchanged. Only S04 is removed from accepted results and will be re-executed.

incidents.reason: Accounting consumer incorrectly preferred a malformed EVAL_BILLIN prompt marker over the exact host-owned exclusive unit-relay identity. All five real requests have the same correct owned_accounting_task_id and complete usage. This false attribution failure is an observer oracle defect, not evidence of OpenClaw losing cost records. Only unit 1 is invalidated and rerun; valid units 2-6 remain accepted.
incidents.preservation: Original compact records and manifest preserved under quarantined-results. Immutable native/provider ZIP and all real paid usage remain retained.
incidents.correction: Use exact exclusive host unit ownership first; preserve the original model prompt marker as an observation. Recalibrate and execute only missing unit 1.

incidents.reason: The explicit child continuation incorrectly used generic HTTP completions with a reserved agent:main:subagent namespace. Native HTTP returned its documented reserved-namespace refusal before dispatch. This does not test native child resumption. Replace only S02 with documented operator sessions.send, proving the retained session ID and actual new MCP receipt; S01/S03 remain accepted.
incidents.preservation: Original compact records and manifest preserved under quarantined-results; immutable hosted raw evidence stays unchanged.
incidents.correction: Use documented native sessions.send and verify real child continuation after a fresh full-family calibration. Rerun S02 only.

incidents.reason: Final source/fixture review: OBS-04-S02 had only 128 MiB tmpfs although native verification reserves 256 MiB, preventing the intended archive/reimport boundary. OBS-04-S03 and OBS-06-S06 incorrectly required a full synthetic secret in live tool output; native read returned a masked value (SYNTHE…suffix), so the scripted model falsely refused a successful read. Fix the hosted backup space and use an independent plaintext source plus a benign model-visible read marker, retaining whether the live secret is already masked. These records do not establish architecture defects.
incidents.preservation: Original normalized records and manifests preserved under quarantined-results; immutable raw hosted evidence is unchanged.
incidents.correction: Recalibrate native OBS-04/OBS-06 and rerun only these three scenarios.

incidents.reason: The reused-connection adapter sent each token to a different native conversation because Gateway.request defaulted its session key to the token. It never established cross-turn MCP reuse. Fix only this scenario to use one retained native conversation and verify the actual service-side MCP session generation before and after revocation. Original records do not establish a reused-connection revocation defect.
incidents.preservation: Original compact records and manifest remain under quarantined-results; immutable raw hosted evidence is unchanged.
incidents.correction: Use a fixed native conversation for the reused-connection case and rerun only this scenario after full native family calibration.
